body.statement: If \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), and \(\epsilon_n=n^{-2/5}\), then \(q=1/4\), \(D_F=6\), \(\kappa=2/7\), and \(t_s=1/2\). At \(t=2/5\), \(b_n=n^{-2/7}\), \(r_F=n^{-4/15}\), and \(r_G=n^{-3/10}\), so \(r_F\) leads. The choices \(h\asymp n^{-4/15}\) and \(\ell\asymp n^{-16/15}\) give \(\Delta_1(S_{h,\ell})\asymp n^{-2}h^{-1}\ell^{-1}=n^{-2/3}\) and \(W_H(\Pi_+^n,\Pi_-^n)\lesssim abn^2h\ell\), yielding the matched scale \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp n^{-4/15}\).
body.justification: This specialization exposes any missing factor of \(n\), normalization bias, or surviving singleton before the general theorem is attempted.
body.gap: A direct \(n\epsilon_n\) nuisance balance would give the unsupported slower scale \(n^{-3/25}\); this proposition audits the \(n^{-4/15}\) scale implied by the coupled fuzzy balance.
body.consumer: It is a reproducible audit case for sensitivity and transport calculations.
